NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND AGENDA
NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
Tuesday, June 13, 2023
ONE OR MORE SUPERVISORS MAY ATTEND VIA VIDEO AND/OR TELEPHONICALLY 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors will hold a meeting open to the public on Tuesday, June 13, 2023, in the Supervisors’
Chamber in the Navajo County Governmental Complex, 100 East Code Talkers Drive, Holbrook, Arizona. The Board may vote to
meet in a closed executive session to discuss certain matters and for legal advice on any item as indicated on the following
agenda, pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.03(A) (3). 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors finds that it is in the best interest of the community to conduct this public meeting using
a hybrid method in order to serve the public interest. 
Join Zoom Meeting, click here: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87692173340?pwd=WDU3WWhlZFcxd1JqN1BzYXI1dUdpZz09 
 
Call In Number: 1-253-215-8782 OR 1-346-248-7799 (You may use either teleconference number)
Meeting ID: 876 9217 3340
Passcode: 271616
Persons with disabilities who need accommodation to attend or participate in the meeting may contact the Clerk of the Board’s
office at (928) 524-4053; at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, so an accommodation can be arranged.
Items on the agenda may be considered out of order at the Chairman’s discretion. A copy of the agenda background material
provided to the Board, except items to be considered in executive session, is available for public inspection at Navajo County
website, www.navajocountyaz.gov
“NOTICE TO PARENTS AND LEGAL GUARDIANS: Parents and legal guardians have the right to consent before Navajo County makes a video
or voice recording of a minor child, pursuant to A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9). The Navajo County Board of Supervisors regular meetings are recorded and
may be viewed on Navajo County’s website, and social media pages. If you permit your child to attend/participate in a televised Navajo County
Board of Supervisors meeting, a recording will be made, and your child’s picture may be posted on Navajo County’s social media pages. You may
exercise your right not to consent by not allowing your child to attend/participate in the meeting.” 
9:00 a.m. Call To Order: Invocation and Pledge of Allegiance
           
1. CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Individuals may address the Board on any relevant issue for up
to 3 minutes. At the close of the call to the public, Board members may not respond to any
comments but may respond to criticism, ask staff to review a matter or ask that a matter be
placed on a future agenda.
 
 
2. CONSENT AGENDA: These items are considered to be routine or administrative in
nature and will be approved in a single motion. A Board member may request for any item
to be removed from the consent agenda and considered on the regular agenda:
 
 
a. Minutes: May 23, 2023, Regular Meeting Minutes and June 6, 2023, Executive Session
Minutes
 
 
b. Warrant & Voucher Report over $1000, May 2023  
 
c. Constable Reports: Winslow Precinct #2, April 2023

<!-- page 2 -->
d. Award for the Annual Newspaper Advertising and Printing Contract B23-04-018 to Navajo
County Publishers Inc., dba The Tribune
 
 
e. Contracts signed by County Manager/Assistant County Manager pursuant to Board of
Supervisors Resolution: Renewal of HyperVelocity License Agreement for Navajo
County#LIC-NAVAJO-2023-01
 
 
e. Amendment No. 2 to Contract B20-01-030 Bank Services Agreement with Wells Fargo
Bank, N.A. which includes revised pricing for the 4th and 5th year as identified in
Attachment A Treasury Management Proposal
 
 
f. Application for supervised fireworks display permit submitted by the Heber-Overgaard
Chamber of Commerce
 
 
g. Alice's Place has requested $600.00 from the Navajo County Attorney's ARRF monies to
assist with their annual 2023 fundraiser, "Murder Mystery Dinner & Dance"
 
 
h. Approval and Acceptance of the FY24 ACJC BYRNE Grant Agreement #DC-24-029 to
pay partial salaries for two dedicated prosecutors to prosecute drug sales and trafficking
offenses.
 
 
i. Memorandum of Understanding between the Arizona Department of Administration
Technology or State of Arizona 9-1-1 Program and the Navajo County 9-1-1 System
Administrator
 
 
j. Memorandum of Understanding with the Northeastern Arizona 911 User's Association
(NAUA)
 
 
k. Intergovernmental Agreement between Navajo County Sheriff's Office and Claysprings
Pinedale Fire Department for additional emergency communications and radio equipment
 
 
l. Arizona Department of Administration 9-1-1 Program Grant Agreement, Grant Number
ADOA-AZ911-24-12
 
 
m. Intergovernmental Agreement between Holbrook Unified School District #3 and the
Navajo County Sheriff's Office for a 10-month School Resource Deputy's involvement and
participation in their School Safety Program
 
 
n. Reissuance of Stale Dated Checks  
 
o. Resolution Number 18-2023, accepting grant funding from the Gila River Indian
Community for a special response team vehicle for the Joseph City Fire District
 
 
p. Tax exemptions filed pursuant to ARS §42-11153 as a Request for Redemption of Waiver

<!-- page 3 -->
q. Appointment of Tisha Lee Carlisle as Republican Precinct Committeeman for Pioneer
Precinct
 
 
r. Submission of ADOT Encroachment Permit Application for Segment 1 of Broadband
Infrastructure Development Project and granting authority to Capital Projects Manager to
sign this Encroachment Permit Application and all other future Permit Applications
necessary for this project
 
 
s. Legal Services Contracts for the Public Defenders Office with the Law Office of Michael
S. Penrod, PLLC
 
 
3. SHERIFF'S OFFICE:  
 
a. Presentation on the recent completion, dedication, and future upkeep of the Navajo County
Peace Officer Memorial
 
Presented By: John Jarrett
 
4. NAVAJO COUNTY PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES DISTRICT: Board of Directors
Session: 
 
 
a. REGULAR AGENDA:  
 
1. Presentation of the 2023 Wildfire Season Outlook  
Presented By: Catrina Jenkins & Brian Swanty
 
5. SUPERINTENDENT OF SCHOOLS:  
 
a. Consideration of Memorandum of Understanding between the Navajo County Sheriff's
Office and the Superintendent of Schools office to provide educational services in the
Navajo County jail. 
 
Presented By: Jalyn Gerlich
 
6. ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES:  
 
a. Presentation on Navajo County 5K County Health Day Events  
Presented By: Eric Scott
 
b. Consideration and adoption of the proposed Tentative Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-24 for
Navajo County.
 
Presented By: Jayson Vowell
 
c. Board of Directors Sessions for consideration and possible adoption of the Tentative

<!-- page 4 -->
c. Board of Directors Sessions for consideration and possible adoption of the Tentative
Fiscal Year 2023-24 Budgets:
1.  Navajo County Public Health Services District
2.  Navajo County Library District
3.  Navajo County Flood Control District including LCR Flood Control Zone
4.  White Mountain Lakes County Recreation Improvement District
5.  Silver Creek County Road Improvement District
6.  Victory Heights Road Maintenance District
7.  Porter Mountain Domestic Water Improvement District 
8.  Fawnbrook Domestic Water Improvement District  
9.  Joseph City Street Lighting Improvement District
10.  Navajo County Jail District
11. Timberland Acres Special Road District
12. White Mountain Lakes #2 Special Road District
13. Silver Creek Flood Protection District
 
Presented By: Jayson Vowell
 
7. PUBLIC WORKS:  
 
a. Consideration of award of contract B23-04-026 Box Culverts and Footing Forms to
Contech Engineered Solutions.
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
 
b. Consideration of approval for the purchase of one 2011 Caterpillar 120M Motor Grader
from Empire Machinery.
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
 
c. NAVAJO COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT: Board of Directors Session:  
 
1. REGULAR AGENDA:  
 
a. Consideration of approving JE Fuller's contract "Silver Creek Flood ALERT" for
the development of the Silver Creek Flood Alert System in the Silver Creek watershed.
 
Presented By: Bill Bess
 
8. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
 
a. Consideration of Master Subscription Agreement with Granicus for a Webcasting Solution.  
Presented By: Melissa Buckley
 
b. EXECUTIVE SESSION pursuant to A.R.S. §38-431.03(A)(1) for interviews for the
County Manager Position.
 
 
c. RECONVENE: Direction to staff on matters related to the hiring process of the County
Manager position.

<!-- page 5 -->
9. COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE: Report from County Manager, County Attorney and
Board members.
 
 
 
10. ADJOURN  
 
Dated: June 9, 2023 NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
Posted: 8:15 a.m. By: MWB                         
Melissa W. Buckley - Clerk of the Board

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. d.        
Meeting Date: 06/13/2023  
Title: Annual Newspaper Advertising and Printing B23-04-018
Submitted By: Cheryl Hollins, Account Specialist
Department: Board of Supervisors
Motion before the Board:
Award for the Annual Newspaper Advertising and Printing Contract B23-04-018 to Navajo
County Publishers Inc., dba The Tribune
Background:
This is an annual contract for the newspaper advertising and printing which is required per
Statute A.R.S. 11-255.  Sealed bids were received by the Board of Supervisors at the Navajo
County Government Center, Holbrook, Arizona until 3:00 p.m M.S.T, May 24, 2023.  The bids
were publicly opened and read aloud at 3:15 p.m. M.S.T.  Two bids were received and Navajo
County Publishers Inc., dba The Tribune was the lowest responsive, responsible bidder, with a
bid of $1.35 per column inch.
Staff recommends the award of this contract to Navajo County Publishers Inc., dba The Tribune.

CONTRACT FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES 
 
Agreement made as of June 13, 2023, effective July 1, 2023 thr ough June 30, 2024 
between Navajo Count y (“County”) and Navajo Count y Publishers Inc., dba The 
Tribune. (“Consultant”). 
 
Whereas, the County requires certain profe ssional services to provide Annual 
Newspaper Printing and Advertising Pursua nt ARS§ 11-255 (“Project”); with the 
contents of ARS§ 11-217, 11-254.01, 39-201 through 39-205, and 39-221.  
 
Whereas, Consultant represents that it has th e necessary expertise to provide such 
services in accordance with the terms of this Agreement. 
 
Now, Therefore, the parties agree as follows: 
 
1. Services.  Consultant shall perform all work for Annual Contract for Advertising 
and Printing, Contract #B23-04-018, and those additional items set forth in the 
Consultant’s offer and letter dated May 5, 2023, in a competent and professional 
manner to the satisfaction of the County.   The Annual Contr act for Advertising 
and Printing, B23-04-018 and the Consulta nt’s Proposal are attached hereto and 
by this reference incorporated herein.  If  any incorporated term is inconsistent 
with the Agreement, this Agreement shall control.  
 
2. Consultant’s Expertise.  Consultant warrants that it has the ability, authority, 
capacity and professional expertise to perfo rm this agreement.  Consultant shall 
self-perform this agreement and be devot ed to the successful accomplishment of 
the work to be performed hereunder.  Once work commences on this agreement, 
Consultant shall adhere to agreed upon timeline and commitment to successful 
completion of the contracted services. 
 
3. Independent Contractor .  Consultant acknowledges th at it is an independent 
contractor.  Neither party is or shall be an  agent, employee, partner, joint venturer 
or associate of the other.  An employee or agent of one  party shall not be deemed 
an employer or agent of the other party fo r any purpose.  Taxes or Social Security 
contributions will not be  withheld from any pa yment by the County, and 
Consultant shall be solely responsible for such matters.

<!-- page 450 -->
Navajo County ‐ For Official Use Only 
4. Subcontracts.  Consultant shall not enter any subcontract with respect to any of 
the work to be performed hereunder with out the County’s prior written approval.  
All subcontracts shall comply with a pplicable federal a nd state laws and 
regulations and shall impose on the s ubcontractor substantially the same 
obligations as are imposed on Consultant by this Agreement with respect to those 
matters covered by Sections 8, 9, 10, 12, 15 and 18.  Consultant is responsible for 
full performance of this Agreement regardless of whether subcontractors are used. 
 
5. Time for Completion.  Consultant’s services will be provided in a manner 
consistent with the degree of care and skill ordinarily exercised by members of the 
same profession currently practicing unde r similar circumstances.  Consultant’s 
services shall be performed as expeditious ly as is consistent with professional 
skill and care and the orderly progress of the project, and in accordance with the 
agreed upon schedule for the performance of  the services hereunde r.  Time limits 
established by a schedule approved by the County shall not, except for reasonable 
cause, be exceeded by County or Consultant .  The schedule shall be adjusted, if 
necessary, as the project proceeds.  Th e date for final performance shall be 
extended by the number of days that pe rformance is delayed by governmental 
approval or review procedures or other causes beyond the Consultant’s reasonable 
control, as jointly confirmed in writing by the parties’ representatives. 
 
6. Payment.  County shall pay to Consultant a not-to-exceed sum of $1.35 per 
column inch as payment in full for all se rvices rendered by Consultant pursuant to 
this Agreement.  Payments shall be made  within 30 days of County’s receipt of 
Consultant’s monthly invoices.  Each invoice shall detail th e work performed 
during the billing period.  Invoice amounts in percent of project cost shall not 
exceed the percentage of completion of the project as approved by County.   
 
7. Term of Contract.  July 1, 2023 thru June 30, 2024. 
 
8. Defects in Work.   County may reject any work product that fails to meet 
customary professional standards or project  specifications.  Consultant agrees to 
promptly remedy all such deficiencies.  The parties shall make a good faith effort 
to resolve any controversy or claim thro ugh informal negotiation as set forth in 
Section 12.  No compensation shall be paid for any rejected work until such issues 
have been resolved. 
 
9. Insurance Requirements.  There are no insurance requirements for this contract. 
   
10. Indemnity.  To the fullest extent allowable by law, Consultant  shall defend, 
indemnify and hold harmless County and its representatives, officers, officials and 
employees (the “Indemnitees”) from and against all claims, damages, losses and

<!-- page 451 -->

expenses (including but not limited to atto rneys fees, court costs, and the costs of 
appellate proceedings) relatin g to, arising out of or re sulting from Consultant’s 
negligent acts, errors, mistakes or om issions in the performance of this 
Agreement.  Consultant’s duty to defend, hold harmless and indemnify the 
Indemnitees shall arise in connection with any claim, damage, loss or expense that 
is attributable to bodily injury, sickness, di sease, death or injury to, impairment or 
destruction of property including loss of use resulting therefrom cause whole or in 
part by any negligent act, error, mistake or omission in the performance of this 
Agreement (including those by any pers on for whose negligent acts, errors, 
mistakes or omissions Consultant may be liable) to the extent of Consultant’s 
negligence or fault.  The amount and type of insuran ce coverage requirements set 
forth above shall not limit the scope of the indemnity in this paragraph. 
 
11. Records.  Consultant shall retain and sha ll require each subcontractor (if 
applicable) to retain, all books, accounts, reports, files and other records relating 
to this Agreement for a period of five years after completion of the work.  All 
such documents shall be subject to  inspection and audit by County upon 
reasonable notice during normal business hours.  A legible copy of any or all such 
documents shall be produced by Consultant at the request and expense of County. 
 
12. Non-Assignment.  Consultant shall not assign  any right in this Agreement 
without County’s prior writte n approval, nor shall Cons ultant delegate any duty 
hereunder without County’s prior written approval. 
 
13. Negotiation of Disputes.   The parties shall make a good faith effort to resolve 
any claim or controversy or claim throu gh informal negotiation.  Notice of any 
claim or controversy shall be provided in  writing, with supporting documentation, 
to the recipient designated in Section 21.  The recipient shall have seven calendar 
days to prepare and deliver a written res ponse.  If the parties fail to resolve the 
disputes within a reasonable period of not  less than ten days, either party may 
pursue available legal remedies. 
 
14. Suspension and Termination by County: 
 
a. Suspension.  County may, without cause, orde r Consultant in writing to 
suspend, delay or interrupt its performan ce in whole or part.  An adjustment 
shall be made to the completion date  and for any increase in cost of 
performance resulting from the suspensi on, delay or interruption.  No 
adjustment shall be made to the extent  that performance is or would have 
been suspended, delayed or inte rrupted by another cause for which 
Consultant is responsible.

b. Termination for Cause.  County may terminate this Agreement for cause if 
Consultant refuses or fails to perfo rm this Agreement; disregards laws, 
ordinances, rules, regulations or or ders of a public authority having 
jurisdiction; or otherwise commits a ma terial breach of this Agreement.  
When any of the foregoing causes exist, County shall give Consultant written 
notice and a ten-day opportunity to cure the default.  If the default remains 
uncured, County may (without prejudice to any rights or remedies it may 
have) terminate this Agreement and finish the work or cause it to be finished.  
If the unpaid balance of the Agreement exceeds the cost of finishing the work 
(including expenses incurred by the County because of the Consultant’s 
default), Consultant shall be entitled to payment for its performance up to the 
amount of such excess.  If the cost of finishing the work exceeds the unpaid 
balance, Consultant shall pay the difference to County. 
 
c. Termination for Convenience.   County, by written notice to Consultant, 
may terminate this Agreement in whole or  part when in the sole discretion of 
County, it is in County’s best interests to  do so.  Consultant shall be paid for 
all material, equipment and services provided, as well as reasonable 
termination expenses and a reasonable allowance fr om profit and overhead, 
provided that such payments, exclusiv e of termination expenses, shall not 
exceed the total amount payable pursu ant to Section 6 less any payments 
previously made to Consu ltant.  Consultant shall not  be entitled to profit and 
overhead on material, equipment and services which were not provided. 
 
d. Consultant’s Responsibility.  Upon receipt of a termination notice, 
Consultant shall (a) prompt ly discontinue all servi ces (unless notice directs 
otherwise), and (b) deliver or otherwis e make available to County copies of 
all data, reports, summaries and other information and materials developed or 
accumulated by Consultant in performing this Agreement. 
 
15. Termination by Consultant.  Consultant may terminate this Agreement upon 
written notice to County if performance is made impossible for a period of thirty 
(30) consecutive calendar days for any of  the following reasons through no act or 
fault of Consultant or its agents, employ ees or subcontractors:  issuance of an 
order by a count or other public aut hority having jurisdiction; an act of 
government, such as a declarat ion of national emergency; or a natural disaster or 
other Act of God.  Consultant may al so terminate this Agreement upon written 
notice and a ten-day opportunity to cure if County fails to make any payment 
within time set forth in Section 6.  Cons ultant may also terminate this Agreement 
upon written notice if suspensions, delays or  interruptions by County equal in the 
aggregate more than 100% of the total number of days scheduled for completion.

16. Governing Law.  This Agreement shall be governed  by the law of the State of 
Arizona.  Any suit arising out of this Ag reement shall be brought in the state 
courts of Arizona (with venue  in Navajo County) or fe deral district of Arizona, 
but only after informal negotiation pursuant to Section 12. 
 
17. Incorporation of Applicable Laws.   Every provision of law required by statute 
or regulation to be in this Agreement will be read and enforced as though included 
herein.  Each party shall promptly notif y the other upon discovery that any such 
provision has been omitted. 
 
18. Non-Collusion.  The provisions A.R.S. 38-511 are incorporated herein by this 
reference. 
 
19. One-Year Limitation on Actions.  No action shall be maintained by Consultant 
on any claim based upon or arising out of this Agreement unless such action is 
commenced within one year after the County’s final payment hereunder.

 Alerts Service
 Charges are assessed against the volume of Alerts per user, per company, per month basis. Users are only

 per company cap for billing.
  
 Services with No Volumes
 Services listed with zero volume are not included in the estimated monthly analysis fee but are included in the event
 the service is used in the future.

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. h.        
Meeting Date: 06/13/2023  
Title: FY24 ACJC Byrne Grant Agreement #DC-24-029
Submitted For: Brad Carlyon, County Attorney  Submitted By: Lynda Young, Office
Manager
Department: County Attorney
Motion before the Board:
Approval and Acceptance of the FY24 ACJC BYRNE Grant Agreement #DC-24-029 to pay
partial salaries for two dedicated prosecutors to prosecute drug sales and trafficking offenses.
Background:
Through the Byrne grant, we are able to have dedicated attorneys that punish offenders of
drug trafficking in Navajo County. This grant, funded through the Arizona Criminal
Justice Commission, allows our attorneys to work closely with law enforcement, strengthening
collaborations with other agencies, resulting in stronger investigations. We expect to deprive
these dealers and manufacturers from profits through seizures and forfeitures. These efforts will
slow down the drug operations in our county that impact drug-related robbery and theft,
drug-related domestic violence, drug-related child abuse, drugs ripping apart families,
and drugs invading our schools.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: FY24
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: $208,086.7
Fiscal Impact:
Grant award is $135,474.79 with ACJC funding $101,606.10 and a match requirement of
$33,868.70 to be paid out of RICO funds.

I. In the event of a dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating in any way to the Agreement, the
complaining Party shall notify the other Party in writing thereof. Within 30 calendar days of such notice,
representatives of both Parties shall meet at an agreed location to attempt to resolve the dispute in good
faith. Should the dispute not be resolved within 30 calendar days after such notice, the complaining Party
shall seek remedies exclusively through arbitration, in accordance with the provisions of A.R.S. § 12-1501
through 12-1518.
II. The arbitration demand must be a clear and concise statement of the claim or dispute. The respondent's
answer and any counterclaims must be filed within 20 calendar days of service of the demand.
III. The arbitration shall be conducted in Maricopa County.
IV. The arbitration shall be conducted by one arbitrator. If the Parties are not able to agree upon the selection
of an arbitrator, within 20 calendar days of the commencement of an arbitration proceeding by service of a
demand for arbitration, the court on application of a Party shall appoint the arbitrator.
V. The arbitrator must promptly set a conference to clarify the claims and defenses, to establish fair
procedures, and to set a schedule for completing the arbitration.
VI. It is the intent of the parties that, barring extraordinary circumstances, arbitration proceedings will be
concluded with 120 calendar days from the date the arbitrator is appointed. The arbitrator may extend the
time limit in the interests of justice. Failure to adhere to this time limit shall not constitute a basis for
challenging the award.

The Contracting Agency, in consultation with State Risk, reserves the right to review or make modifications to
the insurance limits, required coverages, or endorsements throughout the life of this contract, as deemed
necessary. Such action will not require a formal Contract amendment but may be made by administrative
action.
Exceptions:
In the event the Contractor or subcontractor(s) is/are a public entity, then the Insurance Requirements shall
not apply. Such public entity shall provide a certificate of self-insurance. If the Contractor or subcontractor(s)
is/are a State of Arizona agency, board, commission, or university, none of the above shall apply.

ELECTRONIC RECORD AND SIGNATURE DISCLOSURE  
From time to time, Arizona Criminal Justice Commission (we, us or Company) may be required 
by law to provide to you certain written notices or disclosures. Described below are the terms 
and conditions for providing to you such notices and disclosures electronically through the 
DocuSign system. Please read the information below carefully and thoroughly, and if you can 
access this information electronically to your satisfaction and agree to this Electronic Record and 
Signature Disclosure (ERSD), please confirm your agreement by selecting the check-box next to 
‘I agree to use electronic records and signatures’ before clicking ‘CONTINUE’ within the 
DocuSign system. 
 
Getting paper copies  
At any time, you may request from us a paper copy of any record provided or made available 
electronically to you by us. You will have the ability to download and print documents we send 
to you through the DocuSign system during and immediately after the signing session and, if you 
elect to create a DocuSign account, you may access the documents for a limited period of time 
(usually 30 days) after such documents are first sent to you. After such time, if you wish for us to 
send you paper copies of any such documents from our office to you, you will be charged a 
$0.00 per-page fee. You may request delivery of such paper copies from us by following the 
procedure described below. 
 
Withdrawing your consent  
If you decide to receive notices and disclosures from us electronically, you may at any time 
change your mind and tell us that thereafter you want to receive required notices and disclosures 
only in paper format. How you must inform us of your decision to receive future notices and 
disclosure in paper format and withdraw your consent to receive notices and disclosures 
electronically is described below. 
 
Consequences of changing your mind  
If you elect to receive required notices and disclosures only in paper format, it will slow the 
speed at which we can complete certain steps in transactions with you and delivering services to 
you because we will need first to send the required notices or disclosures to you in paper format, 
and then wait until we receive back from you your acknowledgment of your receipt of such 
paper notices or disclosures. Further, you will no longer be able to use the DocuSign system to 
receive required notices and consents electronically from us or to sign electronically documents 
from us. 
 
All notices and disclosures will be sent to you electronically

Edward Byrne Justice Assistance Grant Program FY 2021 Local Solicitation 
Certifications and Assurances by the Chief Executive of the Applicant Government 
On behalf of the applicant unit of local government named below, in support of that locality’s application for an award 
under the FY 2021 Edward Byrne Justice Assistance Grant (“JAG”) Program, and further to 34 U.S.C. § 10153(a), I 
certify to the Office of Justice Programs (“OJP”), U.S. Department of Justice (“USDOJ”), that all of the following are 
true and correct: 
1. I am the chief executive of the applicant unit of local government named below, and I have the authority to make 
the following representations on my own behalf as chief executive and on behalf of the applicant unit of local 
government. I understand that these representations will be relied upon as material in any OJP decision to make 
an award, under the application described above, to the applicant unit of local government. 
2. I certify that no federal funds made available by the award (if any) that OJP makes based on the application 
described above will be used to supplant local funds, but will be used to increase the amounts of such funds 
that would, in the absence of federal funds, be made available for law enforcement activities. 
3. I assure that the application described above (and any amendment to that application) was submitted for review 
to the governing body of the unit of local government (e.g., city council or county commission), or to an 
organization designated by that governing body, not less than 30 days before the date of this certification. 
4. I assure that, before the date of this certification— (a) the application described above (and any amendment to 
that application) was made public; and (b) an opportunity to comment on that application (or amendment) was 
provided to citizens and to neighborhood or community-based organizations, to the extent applicable law or 
established procedure made such an opportunity available. 
5. I assure that, for each fiscal year of the award (if any) that OJP makes based on the application described 
above, the applicant unit of local government will maintain and report such data, records, and information 
(programmatic and financial), as OJP may reasonably require. 
6. I have carefully reviewed 34 U.S.C. § 10153(a)(5), and, with respect to the programs to be funded by the 
award (if any), I hereby make the certification required by section 10153(a)(5), as to each of the items specified 
therein.

9-1-1
Submitted For: David Clouse, Sheriff

Department: Sheriff 
Motion before the Board:
Memorandum of Understanding between the Arizona Department of Administration
Technology or State of Arizona 9-1-1 Program and the Navajo County 9-1-1 System
Administrator
Background:
The Navajo County Sheriff's Office Dispatch Supervisor, Caitlin Montoya, is the System
Administrator for Navajo and Apache County's Department of Administration's State 9-1-1
program.  One of the primary duties for the9-1-1 System Administration is processing all bills
associated with the 9-1-1 network, maintenance, 9-1-1 equipment and special projects funded by
State 9-1-1. In addition to these duties, beginning July 1, 2023, she will be responsible for
processing payments to the service provider, a function that previously belonged to the State
9-1-1 Office.  Prior to this change being implemented, a Memorandum of Understanding is
being presented to each township's City Council and/or Board of Supervisors. This MOU
documents all expectations and processes. Failure for consideration and support of this MOU
may prevent an invoice from being processed.

procedure, outlines the responsibilities of the Sheriff's Office for payment of 9-1-1 related
expenditures and is effective 7/1/2022 and/or upon execution of this contract and shall remain in

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. k.        
Meeting Date: 06/13/2023  
Title: Intergovernmental Agreement between NCSO and Claysprings Pinedale Fire
Department
Submitted For: David Clouse, Sheriff 
Submitted By: Kimberley Willis, Sheriff's Office Finance Manager
Department: Sheriff 
Motion before the Board:
Intergovernmental Agreement between Navajo County Sheriff's Office and Claysprings
Pinedale Fire Department for additional emergency communications and radio equipment
Background:
The Claysprings Pinedal Fire Department (CPFD), a designated Fire District within the County
of Navajo, State of Arizona, and the Navajo County Sheriff's Office (NCSO), a political
subdivision of the County of Navajo in the State of Arizona, wish to enter into an
Intergovernmental Agreement which would allow NCSO to install radio equipment on the radio
tower and shelter on the existing radio tower/shelter owned and operated by CPFD.  By
installing additional emergency communications and radio equipment, NCSO can improve and
expand it's dispatching radio and communication coverage and capabilities for the purpose of
dispatching first responders.
NCSO will lease space within the shelter and on the tower at the rate of $750.00 per year.  The
term of this agreement shall be one year from the effective date of June 1, 2023 to May 31,
2024.  NCSO and CPFD anticipate that this will be a long-term relationship and that this IGA
will be renewed from year-to-year for an indefinite number of terms.

and Apache County's Arizona Department of Administration (ADOA) State 9-1-1 program.

Office for payment of 9-1-1 related expenditures in the amount of $229,052.  The term of the
agreement is from July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024.

Motion before the Board:
Intergovernmental Agreement between Holbrook Unified School District #3 and the Navajo
County Sheriff's Office for a 10-month School Resource Deputy's involvement and participation
in their School Safety Program
Background:
The Holbrook School District has once again been awarded grant monies for the funding of a
10-month School Resource Deputy's (SRO) involvement and participation in their School
Safety Program. This program and grant require certain commitments each school year
including but not limited to 180 hours of law-related education, full-time deputy presence on
campus during school hours, weekly activity logs, and utilization of a multidisciplinary School
Safety Assessment and Prevention Team. The term of this agreement is for fiscal year
2023-2024, and renewable annually for up to 3 years, ending May 31, 2026. A School Safety
Program Cooperative Agreement has been entered into between the parties and is attached.

RESOLUTION ____-23 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS TO 
ACCEPT GRANT FUNDING FROM THE GILA RIVER INDIAN COMMUNITY FOR A 
SEPCIAL RESPONSE TEAM VEHICLE FOR THE JOSEPH CITY FIRE DISTRICT 
 
WHEREAS, the Joseph City Fire District seeks to obtain a vehicle for their Special Response 
Team with the assistance of grant funding; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Joseph City Fire District completed the detailed process of researching, 
compiling, and processing all of the required information to complete the grant application for 
the Gila River Indian Community grant process; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors acting as the sponsoring government 
entity of the grant application, encourages and supports this process of grant funding; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Joseph City Fire District has completed the Gila River Indian Community 
Grant Application meeting the priority areas identified in the grant application for awarding of 
grant funding to government entities; and  
 
WHEREAS, the grant awarded will serve the Joseph City Fire District, a certified fire district in 
Navajo County and the State of Arizona; and  
 
WHEREAS, it is the desire of the Navajo County Board of Supervisors to support and accept 
the awarded grant for the Joseph City Fire District by the Gila River Indian Community; and  
 
WHEREAS, it is the desire of the Navajo County Board of Supervisors to offer their 
appreciation to the Gila River Indian Community for their generosity in offering the grant 
opportunities to agencies in Navajo County and the State of Arizona; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Gila River Indian Community grant application and award process requires a 
resolution from the Navajo County Board of Supervisors to complete the grant award process 
and final award of the grant.  
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Navajo County Board of Supervisors does 
hereby lend its full support and approval, and accepts the awarded amount of the grant, as the 
sponsoring entity for the Joseph City Fire District, by the Gila River Indian Community for the 
purchase of a special response team vehicle.

Appointment of Tisha Lee Carlisle as Republican Precinct Committeeman for Pioneer Precinct
Background:
Appointment valid through Oct. 1, 2024. 16-821. County committee; vacancy in office of
precinct committeeman B. The board of supervisors upon the recommendation of the county
chairman, or the recommendation of a committee designated in the bylaws of the county
committee for that purpose, shall determine when a vacancy exists in the office of precinct
committeeman. If a vacancy exists, the vacancy shall be filled by the board of supervisors from
a list of names submitted by the county chairman of the appropriate political party. Only a
precinct committeeman elected at the primary election prior to the date of a state or county
committee organizing meeting shall be permitted to vote at such meeting. The criteria used to
establish when a vacancy exists in the office of precinct committeeman shall be as established in
section 38-291.      16-822. Precinct committeemen; eligibility; vacancy; duties; term. Any
member of a recognized political party who is a registered voter in the precinct is eligible to
seek the office of precinct committeeman of that party in that precinct. F. The term of office of
a precinct committeeman is two years and begins on October 1 after the primary election at
which the precinct committeeman was a candidate and continues until October 1 after the
following primary election at which a precinct committeeman is elected.

Title: ADOT Encroachment Permit Application for Broadband
Submitted For: Grant Evans, Capital Projects Manager 
Submitted By: Grant Evans, Capital Projects Manager
Department: Public Works
Motion before the Board:
Submission of ADOT Encroachment Permit Application for Segment 1 of Broadband
Infrastructure Development Project and granting authority to Capital Projects Manager to sign
this Encroachment Permit Application and all other future Permit Applications necessary for
this project
Background:
The County's Broadband Infrastructure Development Project includes the construction of
approximately 105 miles of middle mile fiber optic infrastructure along major corridors
throughout the County.  Our partner, eX2, has broken the project up into 6 segments.  By taking
this segmented approach, the design and permitting process is accelerated by securing permits
on the first segments while the remaining segments are being designed.  The County and eX2
must secure the necessary permits from each agency that has permitting jurisdiction over the
rights-of-ways that the alignment follows.  Segment 1 of the project commences near the Cholla
Power Plant in Joseph City and runs east along Interstate 40 to Holbrook, for which ADOT is
the permitting jurisdiction.

I. GENERAL STATEMENT 
This Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made this 13th day of June 2023 with the Law Office of 
Michael S. Penrod, PLLC. an attorney licensed with the State Bar of Arizona, and Navajo County, 
a political subdivision of the State of Arizona, (“County”), PO BOX 668, Holbrook, AZ 86025, for 
professional legal defense services from June 13, 2023 through June 12,  2024.  Attorney has 
professional duties consistent with the Rules of Professional Conduct in providing legal services 
for persons found to be indigent or for whom the Court is required to provide legal counsel in 
Navajo County. 
 
By signing this Agreement, the attorney agr ees to maintain the credentials and business 
permits necessary to practice law in the courts of the State of Arizona and to do so in a competent, 
professional, ethical manner and as an officer of the Court at a ll times. The Attorney warrants 
that he/she is licensed to practice law in the State of Arizona, in good standing with the Arizona 
State Bar and is competent to handle all matters contemplated by this Ag reement in a prompt 
and professional manner on behalf of their clients. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to the Court to be prepared, prompt, comply with court rules, submit 
timely reports, attend meetings with the Court,  accept appointments within the categories of 
assignment as well as those outside the categories when circumstances required, and complete 
cases assigned during the term of the contract. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to his/her clients to keep them advised of the status of their cases, 
be available for consultation, and to diligently represent their interests. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to opposing counsel  to cooperate with scheduling and prompt 
disposition of the case. 
 
II. TERM OF AGREEMENT 
 
A. Period Covered: It is understood between the Attorney and the County that the Attorney will 
accept appointments to represent persons found to be indigent or for whom the Court is 
required to provide legal couns el in Navajo County, from  June 13, 2023 through June 12, 
2024 consistent with the terms of this agreement. This is an annual contract. 
 
B. Termination: Upon thirty (30) days written notice, either party may terminate this agreement 
without cause. The Attorney would be expected to complete any assignments made prior to 
such termination. 
 
C. Renewability: This contract agreement c an be renewed up to (4) additional one-year 
extensions upon mutual agreement from both parties.   
 
D. Indemnification: The Attorney shall at al l times indemnify, defend and hold harmless the 
County and/or any of its agents, officials and employees from any and all claims, demands, 
suits, actions, proceedings, laws, costs and/or damages of every kind and description

the parties.

A. Compensation: The Attorney agrees to provide legal services for the sum of $2,000.00 per 
month.     
 
B. Local Availability: The County and the Court expect the Attorney will be fully prepared to 
provide effective representation to  clients and at appropriate level of service to the courts.   
The Attorney shall also designate an Emergency Contact who can provide basic case 
information on an as needed bases and have author ity to access and transfer case files if 
needed.  It is understood and agreed Attorney shall establish and maintain communications 
capability which will allow prompt receipt of and responses to electronic communications, 
including, but not limited to telephone, e-mail and facsimile, and Attorney will be available to 
receive and promptly respond to such communications.  The Attorney further agrees to be 
physically present in Navajo County at such times and in such locations as may be required 
to make court appearances and to meet with clients, justice syst em personnel and other 
parties as necessary, or to make provisions for substitute representation as specified in 
Section III (E) of this Agreement.

D. Substitute Representation: The parties contemplate, unless otherwise specifically provided

pursuant to this Agreement ar e to be provided by the designat ed Attorney.  The parties 
understand and agree from time to time, illness,  vacation or other circumstances may

shall be the responsibility of the Attorney to provide qualified substitute representation at no

dependencies and delinquencies, guardianship and conservatorship cases to the County 
are subject to prior approval by  County Administration.  The A ttorney shall not broker or

If Attorney is unable to provide service to cases or substitute representation for an

E. Court Payment of Costs and Expenses: 
 
1. Routine Expenses: Routine expense such as  photocopying, postage, travel, office 
supplies, secretarial or other staff services, transcripts of witness interviews or any other 
type of expense that involves the general cost of doing business and other operating 
expenses are not reimbursed by the County and are a personal expense of the attorney. 
This includes hiring a private investigator or any other routine expenses. 
2. Requests for Expenditures: Attorney shall su bmit for prior approval by the Contract 
Administrator (Public Defender) all requests for payment of expert witness fees, travel 
expenses, publication of legal notices, investigators, service of process, court transcript 
fees and other reasonable and necessary expendi tures. Attorney may not incur any 
expense for the account of the County wi thout prior approval of the Contract 
Administrator. Failure to obtain prior a pproval may result in non-payment for the 
expenditure and the debt shall become the per sonal responsibility of the Attorney. A 
copy of the approval must be given to the approved vendor for its billing purposes prior 
to the commencement of their work. If  an approved vendor exceeds the Contract 
Administrator approved amount for the expenditure, the County is not obligated to pay 
any such overage and it becomes the personal  responsibility of the Attorney. When 
billing for reimbursement, receipts for all expenses must be included. All expenses must 
be approved by the Contract Administrator pr ior to being incurred. Bills for expenses 
incurred prior to approval by the Contract Administrator may not be honored or ratified. 
3. Extraordinary Expenses: Attorney may apply to the Contract Administrator for additional 
fees if, in the judgment of  the Attorney, an assigned case  requires more than the base 
level of service anticipated by this Agreem ent because of the complex or protracted 
nature of the case. All requests for additional  compensation shall be submitted to the 
Public Defender for prior approval.

4. Investigators, Experts, Expert Witnesses: Attorney shall submit for prior approval by the

billings prior to payment by the County. The request shall include the following:

• Name and address of the proposed investigator or expert witness. If there is 
a request for an expert witness, the curriculum vitae must be included 
• A list of the number of essential witnesses requested and the approximate 
hours that will be required 
• Any potential travel time 
• A total amount of funds previously received 
• A current financial affidavit 
• A proposed order 
5. Prior Approval: Failure to obtain prior appr oval will result in non-payment for any 
expenditure and the debt shall become the pers onal responsibility of the Attorney.  At 
the sole discretion of the Public Defender, any such non-approved costs with are 
incurred, may be paid and deducted from am ounts otherwise due and owing to the 
Attorney.   
6. Costs Which Could Have Been Avoided:  Court expenses which could have been 
avoided had the attorney been prepared, such as ju ry costs for a trial that is cancelled 
due to acts attributable solely to the defense attorney, Rule 11 evaluation costs for which 
the defendant did not show because of failure of the attorney to timely advise defendant 
of the scheduled appointment, expedited tran scripts, etc., may be charged back to the 
attorney as a personal cost. 
 
F. Billing Procedures & Reporting for Legal Services Provided by Indigents: The Attorney should 
submit a monthly invoice for eac h month’s services. The invoice shall list the names of the 
cases.  Invoices are to be submitted no earlier than the 10th day of the month in which services 
are provided.  Timekeeping is not required.   
 
IV. CASE ASSIGNMENT, CONFLICTS, REASSIGNMENT 
 
A. Case Assignment: The Attorney will be responsible for the Winslow Justice Court caseload 
ordinarily assigned to the Public Defender’s Office.  The Attorney will take over the current 
caseload for that area and directly receive new cases.  This caseload is heard in Winslow, 
AZ every week at 9 a.m. All paperwork will bypass the Public Defender’s Office and instead 
go directly to Attorney’s office.  No conflict check will be performed by the Public Defender’s 
Office because Public Defenders Office will have no paperwork regarding these cases. 
 
B. Conflicts: To accommodate the Court and r educe expense to counsel, conflicts will be 
assigned to another contract Attorney.  
 
C. Reassignment of Case:  I f  the Attorney has been allowed to withdraw because the case is 
assigned to another Attorney, the withdrawn Attorney should promptly turn over his/her case 
file to the new Attorney and notify him/her of any pending hearing dates and the status of the

case. 
 
D. Caseload Limitations: The Agreement does not have a maximum caseload.   
 
E. Reservations: Attorney reserves the right to refuse appointment in cases in which a conflict 
of interest exists or where such appointment  is inconsistent with attorney’s ethical 
responsibilities and/or the Rules of Ethical Conduct. 
 
V. SPECIFIC DUTIES OF COUNSEL 
 
A. Readiness and Promptness for Court: 
 
1. Readiness and Promptness: The Attorney  agrees to be prepared and appear in court 
promptly at or before the time set for hearings and not to rely on Court staff to notify or to 
locate him/her when court is ready to proceed. The Attorney agrees to meet with his/her 
client and discuss the case before the time set for hearing, not at the time set for hearing, 
particularly in those instances in which the client is in custody. 
 
2. Law and Motion Day: The Attorney agrees to be present for Law and Motion Day, status 
conferences, and case management conferences as scheduled. If a substitute Attorney is 
necessary, the Attorney agrees to arrange for and update the substitute on case status so 
the hearing can proceed rather than be continued. 
 
3. Delays: In the event the Attorney will be late due to unforeseen circumstances, he/she 
agrees to communicate the delay and an anticipated arrival time as soon as practicable. 
 
B. Insurance: 
 
1. Liability Insurance: Attorney agrees as a mate rial condition of this  Agreement that each 
shall provide and maintain professional liabi lity insurance in t he minimum amount of 
$100,000.00 per claim, $300,000.00 in the aggregate. The Atto rney shall provide the 
Public Defender with a copy of current certificates of insurance. Failure on the part of the 
Attorney to procure and maintain current liabi lity insurance and provide proof thereof to 
the County shall constitute a material br each of the Agreement  upon which the County 
may immediately terminate the Agreement.    
 
C. Interpreters: 
 
1. Notice: The Attorney should give the Cou rt at least two weeks advance notice, where 
possible, when an interpreter will be necessary to ensure an interpreter can be 
scheduled. 
 
2. Permission: The Attorney should request court permission in advance to use an 
interpreter at court expense for interviews, depositions, etc. 
 
3. Attorney Presence: The Attorney should be present with the interpreter during 
interviews, depositions, and attorney-client discussions.

1. Office: The Attorney agrees to maintain  regular office hours and have a method for 
clients to contact him/her in an emergency outside of regular office hours. Attorney’s 
office shall be staffed by clerical person nel a minimum of twenty (20) hours per week.  
Failure to maintain office staffing shall c onstitute a material breach of the Agreement 
upon which the County may immediately terminate the Agreement. 
 
2. Communication and Representation: The Attorney agrees to promptly return phone calls 
and respond to correspondence, to obtain cl ients’ consent before requesting that 
hearings be rescheduled, to interview witnesses, to issue subpoenas, and in other ways 
deal professionally with the client and diligently represent the client’s interests. 
 
3. Calendar: The Attorney agrees to maintain an accurate calendaring system for all his/her 
cases and to calendar all cases schedule for hearing. Counsel should not rely on court 
staff to advise what is scheduled for him/ her each week. Attorney agrees to be the 
primary source of case information for the client. 
 
4. Completion of Case: Attorney agrees to cont inue to represent any client on cases in 
which the firm was appointed during the term  of this Agreement until the case is 
completed or he/she is relieved of that representation by order of the Court, regardless 
of the termination of the Agreement. 
 
F. Attorney Files: The Attorney should retain his/her file for no less than five (5) years after the 
last action is taken in the case.

professional legal defense services from June 13, 2023 through June 12,  2024.  Attorney has 
professional duties consistent with the Rules of Professional Conduct in providing legal services 
for persons found to be indigent or for whom the Court is required to provide legal counsel in 
Navajo County. 
 
By signing this Agreement, the attorney agr ees to maintain the credentials and business 
permits necessary to practice law in the courts of the State of Arizona and to do so in a competent, 
professional, ethical manner and as an officer of the Court at a ll times. The Attorney warrants 
that he/she is licensed to practice law in the State of Arizona, in good standing with the Arizona 
State Bar and is competent to handle all matters contemplated by this Ag reement in a prompt 
and professional manner on behalf of their clients. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to the Court to be prepared, prompt, comply with court rules, submit 
timely reports, attend meetings with the Court,  accept appointments within the categories of 
assignment as well as those outside the categories when circumstances required, and complete 
cases assigned during the term of the contract. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to his/her clients to keep them advised of the status of their cases, 
be available for consultation, and to diligently represent their interests. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to opposing counsel  to cooperate with scheduling and prompt 
disposition of the case.

accept appointments to represent persons found to be indigent or for whom the Court is 
required to provide legal couns el in Navajo County, from  June 13, 2023 through June 12, 
2024 consistent with the terms of this agreement. This is an annual contract. 
 
B. Termination: Upon thirty (30) days written notice, either party may terminate this agreement 
without cause. The Attorney would be expected to complete any assignments made prior to 
such termination. 
 
C. Renewability: This contract agreement c an be renewed up to (4) additional one-year 
extensions upon mutual agreement from both parties.

E. Court Payment of Costs and Expenses: 
 
1. Routine Expenses: Routine expense such as  photocopying, postage, travel, office 
supplies, secretarial or other staff services, transcripts of witness interviews or any other 
type of expense that involves the general cost of doing business and other operating 
expenses are not reimbursed by the County and are a personal expense of the attorney. 
This includes hiring a private investigator or any other routine expenses. 
2. Requests for Expenditures: Attorney shall su bmit for prior approval by the Contract 
Administrator (Public Defender) all requests for payment of expert witness fees, travel 
expenses, publication of legal notices, investigators, service of process, court transcript 
fees and other reasonable and necessary expendi tures. Attorney may not incur any 
expense for the account of the County wi thout prior approval of the Contract 
Administrator. Failure to obtain prior a pproval may result in non-payment for the 
expenditure and the debt shall become the per sonal responsibility of the Attorney. A 
copy of the approval must be given to the approved vendor for its billing purposes prior 
to the commencement of their work. If  an approved vendor exceeds the Contract 
Administrator approved amount for the expenditure, the County is not obligated to pay 
any such overage and it becomes the personal  responsibility of the Attorney. When 
billing for reimbursement, receipts for all expenses must be included. All expenses must 
be approved by the Contract Administrator pr ior to being incurred. Bills for expenses 
incurred prior to approval by the Contract Administrator may not be honored or ratified. 
3. Extraordinary Expenses: Attorney may apply to the Contract Administrator for additional 
fees if, in the judgment of  the Attorney, an assigned case  requires more than the base 
level of service anticipated by this Agreem ent because of the complex or protracted 
nature of the case. All requests for additional  compensation shall be submitted to the 
Public Defender for prior approval.

attorney as a personal cost.

are provided.  Timekeeping is not required.   
 
IV. CASE ASSIGNMENT, CONFLICTS, REASSIGNMENT 
 
A. Case Assignment: The Attorney will be responsible for the Holbrook Justice Court caseload 
ordinarily assigned to the Public Defender’s Office.  The Attorney will take over the current 
caseload for that area and directly receive new cases.  This caseload is heard in Holbrook, 
AZ every week at 9 a.m. All paperwork will bypass the Public Defender’s Office and instead 
go directly to Attorney’s office.  No conflict check will be performed by the Public Defender’s 
Office because Public Defenders Office will have no paperwork regarding these cases. 
 
B. Conflicts: To accommodate the Court and r educe expense to counsel, conflicts will be 
assigned to another contract Attorney.

file to the new Attorney and notify him/her of any pending hearing dates and the status of the

V. SPECIFIC DUTIES OF COUNSEL 
 
A. Readiness and Promptness for Court: 
 
1. Readiness and Promptness: The Attorney  agrees to be prepared and appear in court 
promptly at or before the time set for hearings and not to rely on Court staff to notify or to 
locate him/her when court is ready to proceed. The Attorney agrees to meet with his/her 
client and discuss the case before the time set for hearing, not at the time set for hearing, 
particularly in those instances in which the client is in custody. 
 
2. Law and Motion Day: The Attorney agrees to be present for Law and Motion Day, status 
conferences, and case management conferences as scheduled. If a substitute Attorney is 
necessary, the Attorney agrees to arrange for and update the substitute on case status so 
the hearing can proceed rather than be continued. 
 
3. Delays: In the event the Attorney will be late due to unforeseen circumstances, he/she 
agrees to communicate the delay and an anticipated arrival time as soon as practicable. 
 
B. Insurance: 
 
1. Liability Insurance: Attorney agrees as a mate rial condition of this  Agreement that each 
shall provide and maintain professional liabi lity insurance in t he minimum amount of 
$100,000.00 per claim, $300,000.00 in the aggregate. The Atto rney shall provide the 
Public Defender with a copy of current certificates of insurance. Failure on the part of the 
Attorney to procure and maintain current liabi lity insurance and provide proof thereof to 
the County shall constitute a material br each of the Agreement  upon which the County 
may immediately terminate the Agreement.    
 
C. Interpreters: 
 
1. Notice: The Attorney should give the Cou rt at least two weeks advance notice, where 
possible, when an interpreter will be necessary to ensure an interpreter can be 
scheduled. 
 
2. Permission: The Attorney should request court permission in advance to use an 
interpreter at court expense for interviews, depositions, etc. 
 
3. Attorney Presence: The Attorney should be present with the interpreter during 
interviews, depositions, and attorney-client discussions.

D. Meetings with the Court: The Attorney agrees  to attend administrative meetings with the 
Court when, and as scheduled regarding the court calendar, procedures, and contract 
issues. 
 
E. Contact with and Representation of Client: 
 
1. Office: The Attorney agrees to maintain  regular office hours and have a method for 
clients to contact him/her in an emergency outside of regular office hours. Attorney’s 
office shall be staffed by clerical person nel a minimum of twenty (20) hours per week.  
Failure to maintain office staffing shall c onstitute a material breach of the Agreement 
upon which the County may immediately terminate the Agreement. 
 
2. Communication and Representation: The Attorney agrees to promptly return phone calls 
and respond to correspondence, to obtain cl ients’ consent before requesting that 
hearings be rescheduled, to interview witnesses, to issue subpoenas, and in other ways 
deal professionally with the client and diligently represent the client’s interests. 
 
3. Calendar: The Attorney agrees to maintain an accurate calendaring system for all his/her 
cases and to calendar all cases schedule for hearing. Counsel should not rely on court 
staff to advise what is scheduled for him/ her each week. Attorney agrees to be the 
primary source of case information for the client. 
 
4. Completion of Case: Attorney agrees to cont inue to represent any client on cases in 
which the firm was appointed during the term  of this Agreement until the case is 
completed or he/she is relieved of that representation by order of the Court, regardless 
of the termination of the Agreement. 
 
F. Attorney Files: The Attorney should retain his/her file for no less than five (5) years after the 
last action is taken in the case.

I. GENERAL STATEMENT 
This Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made this 13th day of June 2023 with the Law Office of 
Michael S. Penrod, PLLC. an attorney licensed with the State Bar of Arizona, and Navajo County, 
a political subdivision of the State of Arizona, (“County”), PO BOX 668, Holbrook, AZ 86025, for 
professional legal defense services from June 13, 2023 through June 12,  2024.  Attorney has 
professional duties consistent with the Rules of Professional Conduct in providing legal services 
for persons found to be indigent or for whom the Court is required to provide legal counsel in 
Navajo County. 
 
By signing this Agreement, the attorney agr ees to maintain the credentials and business 
permits necessary to practice law in the courts of the State of Arizona and to do so in a competent, 
professional, ethical manner and as an officer of the Court at a ll times. The Attorney warrants 
that he/she is licensed to practice law in the State of Arizona, in good standing with the Arizona 
State Bar and is competent to handle all matters contemplated by this Ag reement in a prompt 
and professional manner on behalf of their clients. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to the Court to be prepared, prompt, comply with court rules, submit 
timely reports, attend meetings with the Court,  accept appointments within the categories of 
assignment as well as those outside the categories when circumstances required, and complete 
cases assigned during the term of the contract. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to his/her clients to keep them advised of the status of their cases, 
be available for consultation, and to diligently represent their interests. 
 
The Attorney has a duty to opposing counsel  to cooperate with scheduling and prompt 
disposition of the case. 
 
II. TERM OF AGREEMENT 
 
A. Period Covered: It is understood between the Attorney and the County that the Attorney will 
accept appointments to represent persons found to be indigent or for whom the Court is 
required to provide legal couns el in Navajo County, from  June 13, 2023 through June 12, 
2024 consistent with the terms of this agreement. This is an annual contract. 
 
B. Termination: Upon thirty (30) days written notice, either party may terminate this agreement 
without cause. The Attorney would be expected to complete any assignments made prior to 
such termination. 
 
C. Renewability: This contract agreement c an be renewed up to (4) additional one-year 
extensions upon mutual agreement from both parties.   
 
D. Indemnification: The Attorney shall at al l times indemnify, defend and hold harmless the 
County and/or any of its agents, officials and employees from any and all claims, demands,

DROUGHT MONITOR 
COMPARISON Current drought status:
April was much drier than normal, with many locations across the 
state marking no measurable precipitation for the month. Slight 
amounts of precipitation were measured in some northern 
locations, like Flagstaff, Page, and Window Rock. Temperatures 
along the northern tier were slightly below average, while the rest 
of the state recorded average to above-average temperatures.
Short-term drought changed minimally in April, with modest 
improvement to Moderate (D1) drought, now found only in 
northwestern Mohave County (1% of state). 
Eighty-two percent of the state remained without short-term 
drought, while Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions persisted in most of 
Yuma and La Paz counties, western Maricopa and Mohave 
counties, and northern Coconino County (17% of state).
Development of El Niño conditions are likely (better than 60% 
chance) during the summer with odds increasing even higher in 
the fall months. As a result, there is a slight tilt in odds that 
monsoon rainfall will be below normal across the southern part of 
the state.

SIGNIFICANT WILDLAND FIRE 
POTENTIAL OUTLOOK

<!-- page 618 -->
Navajo County - For Official Use Only
SIGNIFICANT WILDLAND FIRE 
POTENTIAL OUTLOOK – CONT’D
Below Normal across the northern tier of Arizona into the Four Corners. 
Above Normal from southeastern Arizona eastward into southwestern New 
Mexico. 
Normal elsewhere except Below normal across the eastern plains. Incidents 
of significant large fire activity typically begin to increase in May across nearly 
all lower elevation areas and begin moving into mid and even upper elevation 
areas where dryness is a factor.  
This year, given the elevated moisture the past few months and expected 
active weather pattern, the potential will generally stay lower for most of the 
northwestern half or so of the region with Below Normal also expected 
across the far east. Any kind of elevated activity will be most likely across 
southeastern Arizona into western/southwestern New Mexico.

Memorandum of Understanding 
Between the Navajo County School Superintendent and Navajo County Sheriff  
 
This Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is made and entered into by and between the 
Navajo County School Superintendent (hereinafter "School Superintendent")  and the Navajo 
County Sheriff  (hereinafter referred to as " Sheriff") for the purpose of memorializing their 
agreement on the method of delivery of the jail education program pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-
913.01. 
 
Term 
This MOU and cooperative arrangement will be for the period of July 1, 2023, through June 
30, 2024, and may be extended annually based on appropriate funding. 
 
Obligations of the Partners 
The School Superintendent and the Sheriff acknowledge that no contractual relationship 
is created between them by this  MOU. 
 
Cooperation 
The activities, services, and agreed upon duties are as follows:  
 
Duties of the School Superintendent: 
 
The School Superintendent agrees to:  
 
a. Work in cooperation with the Sheriff and shall agree on the method of delivery of the jail 
education program, pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-913.01. 
 
b. Provide qualified education staff that will ensure the detention education program is aligned 
to the Arizona Standards as defined by criteria established by the State Board of Education. 
 
c. Complete student files to include necessary registration forms and records.  This includes 
recording the registration forms submitted from the jail staff in a timely manner to allow 
students to enroll in school within 48 hours of admission to the facility.  Ensure all 
education information and records are maintained in the  inmate’s education file  at the 
facility consistent with state and federal law. Education staff shall maintain the 
confidentiality of these records pursuant to the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act 
of 1974 (FERPA), 20 U.S.C. § 1232g; FERPA's implementing federal regulations at 34 
CFR Part 99; and A.R.S. § 15-141. 
 
a. Develop policies and procedures for the transfer of educational records of any prisoner 
confined in a county jail who has been transfe rred from a juvenile detention center or from 
any other public agency that has provided educational services to that prisoner.  
 
b. Work in cooperation with the Sheriff to provide a minimum of 225 total instructional days  
for qualifying inmates in the jail education program consisting of a minimum  of 240 
minutes (4 hours) of instructional time pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-913.01(E)(l). Instructors 
shall have the proper certification as required by the Arizona Department of Education.

<!-- page 633 -->
Page 2 of2 
MOU Between the School Superintendent and County Sheriff 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
 
c. Work with the Sheriff to ensure all inmates under 18 years of age are enrolled in the education 
program within 48 hours of admission to the facility pursuant to A.R.S. § 15- 913.01 (E)(l). 
 
d. Work with the Sheriff to ensure all inmates under 18 years of age and prisoners with 
disabilities who are age twenty-one or younger are enrolled in the education program within 
48 hours of admission to the facility pursuant to A.R.S. § 15- 913.01 (E)(l). 
e. Work with the Sheriff to ensure all inmates under who are age twenty -one or younger  and 
not a High School graduate are offered the opportunity to  enroll in the education program 
within 48 hours of admission to the facility pursuant to A.R.S. § 15- 913.01 (E)(l). 
  
 
 
 
Duties of the Sheriff: 
 
The Sheriff agrees to: 
 
a. Work in cooperation with the School Superintendent and shall agree on the method of 
delivery of the jail education program, pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-913.01. 
 
b. Provide Jail staff to complete the educational intake and education registration process for 
all inmates age 21 or younger.  This will be done prior to the required 48 hour enrollment 
requirement following admission to the facility pursuant to A.R.S. § 15- 913.01 (E)(l).   
 
c. Provide Jail staff to work with the School Superintendent’s staff to support the delivery of 
educational program.  Support may include: monitoring education through the schools 
computer based curriculum, delivering packets and reinforcing/reviewing academic content 
as needed.   
 
d. Work in cooperation with the School Superintendent to provide a minimum of 225 total 
instructional days for qualifying inmates in the jail education program consisting of a 
minimum of 240  minutes (4 hours) of instructional time pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-
913.01(E)(l). Instructors shall have the proper certification as required by the Arizona 
Department of Education.  
 
e. Work in cooperation with the School Superintendent to ensure all inmates under 18 years 
of age and prisoners with disabilities who are age twenty-one or younger are enrolled in the 
education program within 48 hours of admission to the facility pursuant to A.R.S. § 15 - 
913.01 (E)(l). 
 
f. Work with the School Superintendent to ensure all inmates under 18 ye ars of age are 
enrolled in the education program within 48 hours of admission to the facility pursuant to 
A.R.S. § 15- 913.01 (E)(l). 
 
g. Work with the School Superintendent  to ensure all inmates under 18 years of age and 
prisoners with disabilities who are age twenty-one or younger are enrolled in the education 
program within 48 hours of admission to the facility pursuant to A.R.S. § 15- 913.01 (E)(l).

<!-- page 634 -->
Page 2 of2 
MOU Between the School Superintendent and County Sheriff 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
 
 
 
 
h. Work with the School Superintendent  to ensure all inmates under who are age twenty -one 
or younger  and not a High School graduate are offered the opportunity to  enroll in the 
education program within 48 hours of admission to the facility pursuant to A.R.S . § 15- 
913.01 (E)(l). 
 
i.  Ensure all detained qualified inmates  attend educational programming as offered and 
required by state and federal law unless an inmate presents an immediate or ongoing security 
risk to self, others or the institution. There shall b e documentation whenever a n inmate is 
excluded from the education program and a copy placed in the inmate's personal file. 
 
Liability 
No liability will arise or be assumed between the School Superintendent and Sheriff as a 
result of this MOU. 
 
Amendment 
This MOU may be amended or supplemented in writing by mutual consent of both parties. 
 
Signatories 
This MOU shall be effective as of the date first written above.

Introduction
Navajo County is a political subdivision of Arizona’s State government
• Promotes public safety (Sheriff’s Office and County Jail, 
County Attorney’s Office, Public Defender, Probation, 
Superior and Justice Courts, Clerk of the Court).
• Builds and maintains roads and transportation infrastructure 
in unincorporated areas (Public Works, Flood Control).
• Supports health and welfare of the community (Public 
Health, Library District, Public Fiduciary, Emergency 
Management, Workforce).

political organizations (Assessor, Elections, Recorder, 
Superintendent of Schools, Treasurer).

As required by statute, a full and complete statement of the County's financial affairs for the
preceding fiscal year are included.  Additionally, an estimate of the amounts required to meet
the County's expenditures of fiscal year 2023-24 is included and has been presented on a
summary schedule of estimated revenues and expenditures in accordance with the Arizona
Office of the Auditor General's prescribed format.

Center, Holbrook, Arizona until 3:00 p.m. M.S.T., May 31, 2023, in strict accordance with
specifications on file in the office of the Navajo County Department of Public Works.  No bids
were accepted after 3:00 p.m. M.S.T. The bids were publicly opened and read aloud at 3:15
p.m.  The bid notification was e-mailed to 6 vendors and only one response was received.
The box culverts and footing forms purchased under this contract will be utilized for the
Bourdon Ranch Road Culvert and Cattle Guard project.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends award of contract B23-04-026 Box Culverts and Footing Forms to Contech
Engineered Solutions.

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. b.        
Meeting Date: 06/13/2023  
Title: District 1 Motor Grader
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Miles Begay, Tribal Government Relations Liaison
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of approval for the purchase of one 2011 Caterpillar 120M Motor Grader from
Empire Machinery.
Background:
Over the years, the County has had a successful partnership with the BIA that involves the
County providing an operator to assist in road maintenance activities within District 1. While
working out a similar partnership with Navajo DOT, County would like to provide a motor
grader that the DOT could utilize when working within Navajo County. If approved, the motor
grader will be owned by the County and procured by District 1 funds.The motor grader would
be utilized to maintain routes within Navajo County and in emergency situations be available to
County staff if needed in first response situations, especially in inclement weather. The City of
Tucson has a contract with Caterpillar, Inc. for the purchase or lease of heavy equipment.
Empire Machinery is a dealer for Caterpillar, Inc and this contract is available for the use of
public and nonprofit agencies that have entered into a Cooperative Purchasing Agreement with
City of Tucson's Department of Procurement or registered with the National IPA. 
 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval to purchase the motor grader

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. c. 1. a.        
Meeting Date: 06/13/2023  
Title: Navajo County Flood Control District - Silver Creek Flood Alert System
Submitted For: Bill Bess, County Engineer/Assistant Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Bill Bess, County Engineer/Assistant Public Works Director
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Bill Bess
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of approving JE Fuller's contract "Silver Creek Flood ALERT" for
the development of the Silver Creek Flood Alert System in the Silver Creek watershed.
Background:
Navajo County Flood Control District has operated numerous rain gauges and flow gauges
in the County for many years. The data provided is used to let staff and residence know
where heavy rains are occurring. 
This contract will authorize JE Fuller to provide their professional services to coordinate with
the National Weather Service (NWS) and the Colorado Basin River Forecast Center
(CBRFC) to develop the new forecast flood alert model for the Silver Creek watershed. JE
Fuller will be installing several new rain gauges and flow gauges to provide additional data
needed for the CBRFC to complete their computer modeling.
JE Fuller will also build a new website to display real-time images, from new and
existing cameras, to show the existing condition of several drainage channels, and/or drainage
structures.  The Navajo County Flood Control website will also include real-time rain gauge
and flow gauge data.
 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval of JE Fuller contract.

Jeanine,  
 
Encoding, Installing of System and Supports Remote Video is all a part of the EASE program - Swagit is the only 
vendor that gives you a choice to let their staff edit and process the video that we would be streaming ‘without 
reaching out to third party vendors’ for service. There is no need to hire any additional employees or assign staff 
additional responsibilities, as everything is done remotely from Swagit’s facilities. Swagit provides a sole-source 
service of an extensible automated streaming engine (EASE) software framework. The EASE application is 
manufactured, leased, and distributed by Swagit alone.  
 
We especially need this because the Clerk of the Board is having to be the IT/AV support during the meeting as 
well as take minutes, run the power point presentations, tend to the Supervisors, the Speakers, the audience and the 
zoom production. We need an IT/AV person and our IT Team is at capacity and cannot run our system for the BOS 
meetings. With Swagit, they provide an IT/AV person for up to 25 meetings a year. This would free up the clerk to 
be more present in the meetings. For Navajo County to hire an IT/AV person, it would cost Navajo County 
$50,000- $60,000 salary plus EOB and the position is not in the budget. Currently I have the IT Director on zoom 
texting me during the meeting asking me to switch the cameras from the Speaker to the Board or vice versa, turn up 
or down the volume because those on zoom cannot hear, turn up microphones for the BOS, let people in the zoom 
meeting, mute people on zoom, turn community members video cameras off on zoom, etc. During Power Point 
Presentations, I cannot touch the computer or the speaker will lose control of advancing the slides. With this new 
webcasting system, Swagit will be controlling the cameras, video etc. We will no longer have zoom, unless the 
members of the BOS cannot be present. Everyone else will click on a link on our website and be able to watch the 
meeting live, but not participate. If folks want to participate, they will need to attend the BOS meeting in person.  
 
Indexing - Swagit also timestamps the agenda after the meeting to create an index after the meeting from the video 
that is then placed on our website and then is easily accessible to everyone without having to request a PRR for the 
information. No other company does the indexing for you. This saves the Clerk’s office a significant amount of 
time. We need this so that community members can access the portion of the meeting that they want/need to view 
without having to view the entire meeting. Right now if folks want a copy of the video, they have to do a PRR and 
we send them the entire video. 
 
Supports major media formats - Social Media Extreme – Swagit sets up all the cameras in the BOS chambers, 
directing meeting and going straight to our website. Can also push to all social media formats. We need this 
because we are moving away from Zoom, however still want to be easily accessible to our community members.  
 
Unlimited Archive Storage - Swagit host all videos on our website and back up on their website. We need this 
because we do not have a lot of backup storage on our Internal Network now.

SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION 
 
Swagit has several one-of-a-kind features that could be used for sole source justification depending on 
the agency’s specific needs, and appreciates the opportunity to provide professional multimedia services, 
specifically live HD streaming, agenda and social media integration, HD broadcast delivery, as well as 
‘hands-free’ video on-demand indexing and archiving.   
 
• Swagit is unique in this industry in that it is a complete video production facility capable of 
providing services supporting all of your video capturing, editing, agenda integration and 
processing. 
 
• With Swagit, all audio/video disk storage, system management and bandwidth intensive delivery
